policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'when there was again a great multitude' renders πάλιν ('again') separately from πολλοῦ; the compound παμπόλλου ('a very great multitude') leaves 'again' untranslated.
ASV 'he called unto him his disciples' has no subject 'Jesus'; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would be named as elsewhere in the chapter (v. 17 'And Jesus perceiving it').
ASV 'his disciples' is its normal rendering of the articular μαθητάς as well as of μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ; the possessive does not distinguish the added αὐτοῦ.
ASV 'and some of them are come from far' has the coordinating 'and' (καί), not the causal 'for' that τινὲς γάρ would require.
ASV 'from far' renders μακρόθεν identically with or without the preceding ἀπό; the English shows no trace of the preposition.
ASV 'are come from far' is a perfect of a verb of coming (ἥκω), excluding εἰσίν, which would yield 'are from far'; ἥκασιν and ἥκουσιν are indistinguishable in English.
ὅτι here is recitative before the direct question 'Whence shall one be able...'; ASV leaves it untranslated either way.
ASV 'And he asked them' renders ἠρώτα and the compound ἐπηρώτα alike; no English distinction.
ASV 'And he commandeth the multitude' keeps the historic present παραγγέλλει; the aorist παρήγγειλεν would be 'commanded', as ASV writes for the aorist ἐκέλευσεν in v. 7.
ASV 'to set before them' renders the present and aorist subjunctives alike; the aspect leaves no mark in the English.
ASV 'having blessed them' has an expressed, unitalicized object answering to αὐτά; the omission would leave the participle absolute ('having blessed').
ASV 'to set these also before them' renders the near demonstrative ταῦτα ('these'), not the pronoun αὐτά ('them') of the RP order.
ASV 'And they ate' renders both an initial καί and a postpositive δέ as 'And'; the connective is not distinguished.
ASV 'And they were about four thousand' has no subject phrase 'they that had eaten' for οἱ φαγόντες.
ASV 'And straightway' renders εὐθύς and εὐθέως identically.
ASV 'doth this generation seek a sign' shows neither the Greek word order nor a distinction between ζητεῖ and the compound ἐπιζητεῖ.
ASV 'verily I say unto you' renders the dative ὑμῖν, which the WH omission lacks.

ASV 'again entering into the boat' expresses the prepositional phrase, excluding the bare πάλιν ἐμβάς; among the rest, word order is invisible in English and ASV supplies 'the' for an anarthrous πλοῖον as freely as for τὸ πλοῖον.
ASV 'they reasoned one with another, saying' renders the added λέγοντες.
ASV text reads the first person 'We have no bread' (ἔχομεν); the third-person ἔχουσιν is relegated to the mapped textual note, 'Some ancient authorities read because they had no bread.'
ASV 'And Jesus perceiving it saith unto them' names the subject, rendering the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
ASV 'have ye your heart hardened?' has no 'yet' answering to the RP Ἔτι, though it renders the earlier οὔπω as 'not yet' in the same verse.
ASV 'baskets full of broken pieces' fixes the English order regardless of whether κλασμάτων precedes or follows πλήρεις.
ASV 'And when the seven' has a connective, excluding the asyndetic omission; ASV renders both καί and δέ as 'And' here.
ASV 'And they say unto him, Seven' keeps the present λέγουσιν with the dative αὐτῷ; οἱ δὲ εἶπον would be a past 'And they said'.
ASV 'Do ye not yet understand?' renders Οὔπω; Πῶς / Πῶς οὐ would give 'How is it that ye do not understand?'
ASV 'And they come unto Bethsaida' has a plural verb, rendering ἔρχονται, not the singular ἔρχεται.
ASV uses 'brought out' for both ἐκφέρω and ἐξάγω; 'brought him out of the village' does not distinguish ἐξήνεγκεν from ἐξήγαγεν.
ASV quotes the question in the second person, 'Seest thou aught?', rendering βλέπεις; βλέπει would give an indirect 'whether he saw aught'.
ASV 'he laid his hands upon his eyes' suits both ἐπέθηκεν and ἔθηκεν, since the following ἐπί carries 'upon' in either case.

ASV 'and he looked stedfastly, and was restored, and saw all things clearly' has the man as subject of three verbs (διέβλεψεν, ἀπεκατέστη, ἐνέβλεπεν); the RP reading would require 'he made him look up'.
ASV 'saw all things clearly' renders the neuter ἅπαντα; the masculine ἅπαντας would be 'saw all men clearly'.
ASV 'to his home' is the same for εἰς οἶκον and εἰς τὸν οἶκον; the article leaves no mark.
ASV ends the command at 'Do not even enter into the village', with nothing for μηδὲ εἴπῃς τινὶ ἐν τῇ κώμῃ.
ASV 'And they told him, saying' renders εἶπαν ('told') with λέγοντες; ἀπεκρίθησαν would be 'answered', and the bare RP reading lacks 'saying'.
This ὅτι is recitative before the reported answer 'John the Baptist'; ASV leaves it untranslated whether present or absent.
ASV's elliptical 'but others, One of the prophets' carries no case marking, so the nominative εἷς and the accusative ἕνα come out alike.
ASV 'And he asked them' renders ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς; λέγει αὐτοῖς would be 'saith unto them', as ASV writes for that phrase elsewhere in the chapter.
ASV 'Peter answereth and saith unto him' begins without a connective; the added δέ would give 'And Peter answering'.
ASV 'be rejected by the elders' renders agency the same for ὑπό and ἀπό.
ASV 'And Peter took him' fixes the English order; the position of αὐτόν relative to ὁ Πέτρος is invisible.
ASV 'rebuked Peter' renders the proper name the same with or without the article.
ASV 'rebuked Peter, and saith' has a finite verb joined by 'and' (καὶ λέγει); the participle λέγων would be 'saying'.
ASV 'If any man would come after me' renders the conditional Εἴ τις; Ὅστις would be 'Whosoever', as ASV writes for ὃς ἐάν in v. 35.
ASV 'would come after me' renders ἐλθεῖν, and reserves 'follow me' for the later ἀκολουθείτω; ἀκολουθεῖν here would duplicate that verb.
ASV 'whosoever' renders ὃς ἐάν and ὃς ἄν alike.
ASV 'his life' is the same for ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ and ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν; neither the reflexive nor the word order surfaces in English.
ASV 'whosoever shall lose his life' suits the future ἀπολέσει and the aorist subjunctive ἀπολέσῃ equally in a relative clause of this kind.
ASV 'his life' is the same for ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ and ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν; no English distinction.
ASV 'shall save it' has no resumptive pronoun answering to the RP οὗτος ('the same shall save it').
ASV 'For what doth it profit a man' is present, rendering ὠφελεῖ, not the future ὠφελήσει ('what shall it profit').
ASV 'a man' renders the generic ἄνθρωπον with or without the article; the article would not be reproduced in this idiom.
ASV 'to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life' has infinitives, excluding the ἐάν clause with finite subjunctives; the remaining two readings are the same Greek.
ASV 'For what should a man give' renders τί γάρ; Ἢ τί would be 'Or what'.
ASV 'what should a man give' is deliberative, rendering the subjunctive δοῖ; the future δώσει would be 'what shall a man give'.
